note: What can become an Airship Goal, split into the three families the light 'Goals review' report never mixes. Family A (collected) comes from the client's tagging-plan JSON, not from this file. Family B (nativeSignals) needs zero client instrumentation. predefinedArchetypes is a MATCHER and a naming standard for families A and C — it is never itself a source of activatable candidates: an Airship predefined event the client does not track is a gap, not a goal. Written in English; the only French strings are archetype aliases, used for fuzzy-matching French event names, never for prose.

funnelStages.label: Acquisition
funnelStages.question: Does the app reach and register the user at all?

funnelStages.label: Activation
funnelStages.question: Does the new user reach the first moment of value, and become reachable?

funnelStages.label: Consideration
funnelStages.question: Does the user show intent short of committing?

funnelStages.label: Conversion
funnelStages.question: Does the user complete the act the business is paid for?

funnelStages.label: Loyalty
funnelStages.question: Does the user come back and deepen the relationship?

funnelStages.label: Retention
funnelStages.question: Does the user keep the app, the permission and the subscription?

configModes.label: Count
configModes.description: Number of times the event, tag change or list subscription fires. The default and always-available mode.
configModes.whenToUse: Any goal whose act is meaningful once. Start here unless you have a reason not to.

configModes.label: Frequency over a period
configModes.description: Reaching a number of occurrences within a fixed period — daily, weekly or monthly.
configModes.whenToUse: Habit and depth-of-usage goals, where doing the act once says little and doing it repeatedly is the business outcome (sessions, content consumption, repeat purchase).
configModes.requires: enough volume for the threshold to separate users rather than include everyone

periods.label: Daily
periods.fits: acts a healthy user performs most days (app open, content consumed)

periods.label: Weekly
periods.fits: acts on a weekly rhythm (grocery run, weekly episode, weekly fixture)

periods.label: Monthly
periods.fits: acts on a monthly or slower rhythm (bill payment, subscription renewal, big-ticket purchase)

configModes.airshipUi: Goal type: frequency, with the period and the target count

configModes.label: Threshold on a numeric property
configModes.description: The goal is met when a number-typed property (or an Airship-native numeric such as time in app) crosses a threshold.
configModes.whenToUse: When the act is not binary and its size is the point: basket over a value, session over a duration, points balance over a tier boundary.
configModes.requires: a property whose collected values are genuinely numeric (kind number or amount in the tagging-plan analysis), or an Airship-native numeric property
configModes.airshipUi: Goal type: numeric property, with the property and the threshold

nativeSignals.name: Channel registration
nativeSignals.description: A new device or web channel registers with Airship — the platform-side equivalent of an install that produced an addressable channel.
nativeSignals.whyItMatters: The only acquisition-stage goal available with no client instrumentation at all. It measures whether a campaign produced reachable channels, not just downloads.
nativeSignals.caveat: Counts channels, not people: one user with a phone and a tablet registers twice.

nativeSignals.name: First app open
nativeSignals.description: The first time a given channel opens the app.
nativeSignals.whyItMatters: Separates 'installed' from 'actually started', which is where most onboarding journeys are judged.
nativeSignals.caveat: Fires once per channel, so frequency modes are meaningless on it.

nativeSignals.name: App open
nativeSignals.description: Any app open, from any origin (direct, push, deep link).
nativeSignals.whyItMatters: The cheapest habit metric there is, and the one goal every project can configure on day one.
nativeSignals.caveat: As a plain count it is close to universal and discriminates almost nothing — use a frequency threshold, or it becomes a vanity goal.

nativeSignals.name: Notification opt-in
nativeSignals.description: The user grants push notification permission.
nativeSignals.whyItMatters: Turns the permission ask into a measurable outcome, so a priming in-app or an opt-in journey can be attributed instead of argued about.

nativeSignals.name: First notification opt-in
nativeSignals.description: The first time a channel ever opts in, as opposed to a re-opt-in after a lapse.
nativeSignals.whyItMatters: The right denominator for onboarding permission work: it excludes users who toggled the permission back on later.

nativeSignals.name: Named user association
nativeSignals.description: A channel is associated with a named user — the user logs in, links an account, or creates one.
nativeSignals.whyItMatters: Identity is the precondition for cross-channel messaging, CRM data and any contact-level personalisation. It is usually the single most under-measured step in the funnel.
nativeSignals.caveat: Measures the association, not the account creation itself — a client who needs to tell signup apart from login has to track those as custom events.

nativeSignals.name: Web session
nativeSignals.description: A session on a web channel.
nativeSignals.whyItMatters: The web equivalent of app open, for projects with a web push or web channel presence.
nativeSignals.caveat: Only meaningful when the project actually has web channels.

nativeSignals.name: Uninstall
nativeSignals.description: Airship detects that the app was removed from a channel.
nativeSignals.whyItMatters: The clearest negative outcome available with no instrumentation — useful as a guardrail metric alongside a pressure goal.
nativeSignals.caveat: A negative signal: it belongs in a guardrail, not in the shortlist of goals a campaign is optimised toward.

nativeSignals.name: NPS score
nativeSignals.description: The score a user gives in an Airship Scene NPS survey.
nativeSignals.whyItMatters: Turns sentiment into a goal, and gives a loyalty-stage outcome to brands whose conversion happens off-app.
nativeSignals.caveat: Requires an NPS survey to be published in Scene — no client SDK work, but not zero effort either.

nativeNumericProperties.name: Time in app
nativeNumericProperties.description: Session duration collected by the SDK with no client instrumentation.
nativeNumericProperties.goalUse: Threshold goal for depth of session — 'user spent more than N seconds in app'.

predefinedArchetypes.name: consumed_content
predefinedArchetypes.valueMeaning: duration or completion weight, not currency

predefinedArchetypes.name: purchased
predefinedArchetypes.valueMeaning: order amount in a major currency unit

antipatternRules.label: Technical / debug event
antipatternRules.reason: Instrumentation plumbing, not a business outcome — a goal on it measures the app talking to itself.

antipatternRules.label: Descriptive state, not an act
antipatternRules.reason: Describes what the device or the app is, not something the user did. Excellent for segmentation, meaningless as a goal.

antipatternRules.label: Screen view / impression
antipatternRules.reason: Fires on nearly every session, so almost every user meets it — a goal that everyone reaches ranks nothing.

antipatternRules.label: Negative signal
antipatternRules.reason: The act is an outcome you want to reduce. Track it as a guardrail; optimising campaigns toward it is backwards.

antipatternRules.label: Consent / CMP plumbing
antipatternRules.reason: A regulatory dialogue every user passes through, not a business outcome — the opt-in native signal covers the part that matters.

eventsPerProject.note: Airship keeps up to 1 000 distinct custom event names per project. A taxonomy that sprays event names hits this ceiling and starts dropping the tail.

propertiesPerEvent.note: Up to 100 properties per custom event.

goalsPerProject.note: A per-project ceiling on configured goals exists but the figure moves between releases. Do not quote a number in the report — check Reports > Goals in the dashboard for the project before promising a shortlist size. The prioritisation in this report is a hierarchy, not a quota.

valueSemantics.note: The reserved per-event `value` field takes ONE number. Currency symbols and thousands separators are stripped, so `value` never carries a currency by itself — the currency has to travel as its own property. Treat `value` as a client-declared counter until the collected amounts prove otherwise (decimals, a spread of amounts).

goalReports.name: Goal
goalReports.gives: occurrences of the goal over time

goalReports.name: Channels per goal
goalReports.gives: how many distinct channels reached the goal — the unique-user view a tagging plan cannot give

goalReports.name: Goal frequency per channel
goalReports.gives: how often a single channel reaches the goal, i.e. depth rather than reach

goalReports.name: Goals per platform
goalReports.gives: the same split by iOS / Android / web

goalReports.name: Goal attribution
goalReports.gives: direct and influenced goal completions attributed to each message, journey and Scene
